annotation.title_clean: The challenges and opportunities of artificial intelligence in implementing trustworthy robotics and autonomous systems
annotation.title_en: The challenges and opportunities of artificial intelligence in implementing trustworthy robotics and autonomous systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: He, H.; Gray, J.; Cangelosi, A.; Meng, Q.; McGinnity, T.M.; Mehnen, J.
annotation.summary_en: Review paper on how AI can improve and threaten the trustworthiness of robots and autonomous systems, structured around health/robustness, safety, cybersecurity and human-machine interaction. It proposes an acceptance model and argues human-centred AI should be central to trustworthy RAS. Largely technical, with little formal governance content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Trustworthy RAS require robustness (health), safety, security and trusted human-machine interaction.
Proposes an acceptance model linking reliability, security, safety, privacy and HMI to trust.
AI improves fault detection and cybersecurity but ML is vulnerable to adversarial examples.
Human-centred AI is proposed as the core of trustworthy RAS.
Notes NIST cyber-physical systems trustworthiness framework and GDPR compliance as references.
